notes: Taught managent to schedule duties and gate landmarks on them (docs/infra/duties.md). Recognition choice: a row is a duty when its bundle meta header carries a `duty` key, or `managent add <id> --duty` is used; either sets a stored `duty` flag (so status/next/landmark never re-read bundles). A one-time migration (_sys.duty_migrated) re-derives the flag from bundle headers for the three pre-registered duties (DCLAIM/DRPLAY/DARGUS), whose bundle headers now carry duty=1; DARGUS's deliverable was also corrected from findings/DOCTOR-chunk.json to findings/DARGUS-chunk.json to match its renamed UID. Due-count is closes-based: _sys.closes increments on each task close (done); each duty stores last_chunk_closes and is due once _sys.closes advances due_after (default 5, per-duty via meta due_after=N) past it. `managent duty <UID> done --verdict pass|fail --findings <path>` records a chunk (date/verdict/findings, resets the due-count; a duty never closes). `managent landmark <Ln> --declare` refuses (exit 1) while any duty is overdue or its last chunk failed and names each. Duties render in their own `duties` section (text) and as status=duty/duty=true in status --json (so argus's dispatchable scan cannot mistake one for an open task); `next` never hands one out; audit skips task-lifecycle checks on them. Bars (tools/regression-managent-duty.sh, wired into zig build test): all six arms pass against zig-out/bin/managent — 5 closes make a duty due; overdue duty refuses a declaration and is named; null (no duties) declares; a recorded chunk resets the due-count; next never hands out a duty (task-only and duty-only); a last-failed chunk blocks even when not due. Test-first status: NOT red-first — the mechanism was built and smoke-tested incrementally before the regression script existed; the script now asserts the invariants and is the standing gate. Build, do not deploy: the bundle acceptance (tools/regression-managent-integrity.sh) includes a T268 deployed-vs-built stamp check that can only be green after the Orchestrator deploys bin/managent on a drained fleet, so the acceptance is skipped with that reason (recorded on the row). Follow-ups: (1) docs/infra/managent/spec.md still says 'Eighteen commands' and lacks the duty/landmark verbs — add a section; (2) on a fresh clone the pre-existing duty rows will not auto-migrate because their bundles live in untracked/ (gitignored, absent on a fresh clone) — the duty flag is then best committed in tasks.json or the rows re-registered with --duty.
